why: APPEND-ONLY, WRITTEN BY A HUMAN, VERIFIED BY THE BUILD. `renames.json` refuses while an id has vanished from the library; `value-changes.json` refuses while a computed value has moved. This one refuses while a rule inside `scripts/build-indicator-manifest.mjs` withdraws an indicator the committed manifest is already offering. The exemption it replaces was reasoned — a rule the generator applied is not the rename-versus-removal ambiguity, because the reason is written, printed and in the diff — but it removed the only ratchet on catalogue size and nothing took its place: three ordinary indicators were withdrawn behind a new rule and 307 rows were written with `npm test`, `npm run e2e` and `npm run proof` all green, the single trace a stderr line nothing asserts. A host's saved workspace loses `bop` exactly as hard whether the id vanished or was withdrawn. The reason does not have to be invented here — the generator already printed it. It has to be SIGNED. Nothing is ever deleted from this list: it is how a reader knows what the catalogue has stopped offering and on whose word.
form: Each entry is one indicator leaving the catalogue once: `id`, `reason` (why losing it is acceptable, in a sentence — not the generator's own rule restated), and `measuredAt` (the vendor version the withdrawal was decided against). A `reason` that is absent or empty does not count as a declaration.
